mainTopic: Why "טוב" is only in the second דברות, good signs in dreams, and כלאים among birds and sea creatures
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: why does the word "טוב" appear in the second דברות but not the first? רבי תנחום בר חנילאי answers that the first לוחות were going to break, and רב אשי explains that if "good" had been written on them, good would have been cut off from ישראל. Next, the גמרא brings dream teachings. A ט in a dream is a good sign, and after several rejected reasons the גמרא explains that the first ט in the תורה is in the word טוב. Seeing the word הספד written in a dream is also a good sign, because its letters hint to חסו and פדאוהו. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's rule that כלאים applies to wild animals and birds. Rooster, peacock and pheasant are כלאים even though they are raised together, and domestic and wild geese are כלאים because of real differences in how they reproduce. ריש לקיש teaches that crossbreeding sea creatures earns מלקות, learned from the word למינהו. רחבה asks whether driving a goat and a fish together is forbidden, and the גמרא rejects רבינא's comparison to seeds sown across the border, without deciding the question. The פרק שור שנגח את הפרה then ends.

steps.title: The end of the question about the word "good"
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of רבי חנינא בן עגיל's question: why is "טוב" stated in the second דברות and not in the first?
steps.simpleTranslation: [Why, in the second version of the Ten Commandments,] is the word "good" stated in them?
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a question already in progress. רבי חנינא בן עגיל asked why the second version of the דברות says "טוב" when the first version does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דברים, the מצוה of כיבוד אב ואם adds "so that it will be good for you" (למען ייטב לך), but the version in שמות does not. The question is why this extra word of goodness appears only in the second version.

keyTerms.meaning: Good. Here it means the word of goodness in the second דברות

phrases.english: is "good" stated in them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the second set of the דברות, in דברים 5:16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the word "טוב" appears in the second דברות but not in the first.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא admits he doesn't know and sends him elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא says he doesn't even remember whether "טוב" is written there, and sends the asker to רבי תנחום בר חנילאי, a student of רבי יהושע בן לוי, who was an expert in אגדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Before you ask me why "good" is stated there, ask me whether "good" is stated there at all, because I don't know if it is. Go to רבי תנחום בר חנילאי, who was often with רבי יהושע בן לוי, who was an expert in אגדה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא does not answer the question. He honestly says he isn't sure of the wording and points the asker to someone who might know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a humble "I don't know." A real question needs a confirmed text first, and he admits he can't confirm it. He sends the asker to a student of רבי יהושע בן לוי, because this kind of question belongs to אגדה, his area of expertise.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert in the non-legal teachings of the Torah

phrases.english: He said to him: Before you ask me
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי חייא בר אבא, answering רבי חנינא בן עגיל.

phrases.english: why "good" is stated in them,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁאָלֵנִי אִם נֶאֱמַר בָּהֶן ״טוֹב״ אִם לָאו –
phrases.english: ask me whether "good" is stated in them or not,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם נֶאֱמַר בָּהֶן ״טוֹב״ אִם לָאו;
phrases.english: for I do not know whether "good" is stated in them or not;

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָךְ אֵצֶל רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם בַּר חֲנִילַאי,
phrases.english: go to Rabbi Tanchum bar Chanilai,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה רָגִיל אֵצֶל רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי –
phrases.english: who was regularly with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
who was an expert in aggada.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁאַתָּה שׁוֹאֲלֵנִי לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר בָּהֶם ״טוֹב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question by putting it off and sending the asker to another scholar.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No real answer. He is unsure of the wording and refers the asker to רבי תנחום בר חנילאי.

steps.title: רבי תנחום's answer: the first לוחות were going to break
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום didn't hear an answer from רבי יהושע בן לוי himself, but passes on what שמואל בר נחום told him: "טוב" wasn't written in the first לוחות because they were destined to be broken.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to him. רבי תנחום said: I didn't hear this from רבי יהושע בן לוי himself. But שמואל בר נחום (the uncle of רב אחא בר רבי חנינא, or some say the grandfather of רב אחי בר רבי חנינא) told me: because they were destined to be broken.
steps.whatsHappening: The asker goes to רבי תנחום, who gives an answer he received through a chain of teachers. The first לוחות didn't say "טוב" because they were going to be broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer ties the missing word to what happened to the first לוחות: they were smashed after the חטא העגל. At this point we are not yet told why breaking should matter, so the answer still needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: They were destined in the end to be broken

phrases.english: He went to him.
He said to him: From him I did not hear [this],
phrases.notes: "From him" means from רבי יהושע בן לוי himself.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כָּךְ אָמַר לִי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחוּם
phrases.english: but this is what Shmuel bar Nachum told me,

phrases.aramaic: אֲחִי אִמּוֹ שֶׁל רַב אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: the brother of the mother of Rav Acha son of Rabbi Chanina,
and some say the father of the mother
of Rav Achai son of Rabbi Chanina:
Since they were destined to be broken.
phrases.notes: "They" are the first לוחות, which משה broke after the עגל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל לְגַבֵּיהּ. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִמֶּנּוּ לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the referral from Step 2 and gives the first real answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "טוב" was left out of the first לוחות because they were destined to be broken.

steps.title: So what if they were going to break?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the future breaking of the לוחות would be a reason to leave out the word "טוב".
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they were destined to be broken, what difference does that make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי תנחום's answer. It doesn't see how the breaking connects to leaving out the word "good."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 3 links two things, breaking and the missing word, without explaining the link. The גמרא asks for the missing reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: And if they were destined to be broken, what of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the answer given in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer "since they were destined to be broken"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Breaking the לוחות does not obviously explain why the word "טוב" should be left off them.

steps.title: רב אשי: good would have stopped for ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that if "טוב" had been written on the first לוחות, then when they broke, goodness would, חס ושלום, have stopped for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: [Had "good" been written on them, then when they broke,] good would have been cut off from ישראל, God forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the missing reason. Breaking a לוח with "טוב" written on it would have symbolized good being broken off from the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What is written on the לוחות stands for what it describes. So "good" was saved for the second לוחות, which lasted, and goodness stays with ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Would have stopped, been cut off

steps.whatToRemember: "טוב" appears only in the second דברות because the first לוחות were broken. Had "good" been on them, good would have been broken off from ישראל.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
God forbid, good would have ceased from Israel.
phrases.notes: He means: if "good" had been written on the first לוחות and then they broke.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4 by supplying the missing link.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the hidden reasoning behind the earlier answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The breaking of the לוחות seemed unrelated to which words were written on them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Writing "טוב" on לוחות that would be broken would have meant goodness breaking off from ישראל, so it was saved for the second לוחות.

steps.title: Seeing the letter ט in a dream is a good sign
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע teaches that someone who sees the letter ט in a dream has a good sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: One who sees the letter ט in his dream, it is a good sign for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching connected to the word "טוב." Seeing a ט in a dream is a good sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new statement, linked to the earlier discussion by the theme of "טוב," which begins with ט. The reason is not given yet. The גמרא will ask for it next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
One who sees a tet in his dream,
it is a good sign for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הָרוֹאֶה טֵית בַּחֲלוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related teaching that shares the theme of "טוב."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seeing the letter ט in a dream is a good sign.

steps.title: Why is ט good? There is also a scary פסוק with ט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason. If it is because "טוב" begins with ט, one could just as well connect ט to the frightening פסוק in ישעיהו, "וטאטאתיה במטאטא השמד."
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it's because it is written "טוב," then say instead [it hints to]: "And I will sweep it with the broom of destruction."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ט is a good sign. It then attacks the obvious reason by pointing to a פסוק of destruction that is also full of ט's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ט is good only because it begins "טוב," that reasoning is weak. Another פסוק packed with ט's speaks of punishment. So why should a ט point to good and not to destruction?

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because it is written "good,"
say [instead]: "And I will sweep it with the broom of destruction"!
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 14:23

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 6 and challenges the obvious reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that ט is good because "טוב" begins with it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק of destruction is also full of ט's, so a ט could just as easily hint at something bad.

steps.title: Answer: we mean a single ט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the good sign is a single ט, like the one in "טוב." The destruction פסוק has many ט's.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about one ט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. Seeing a single ט hints to "טוב," while the destruction פסוק is marked by many ט's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is the number of ט's. "טוב" has one ט, and the ישעיהו פסוק has several packed together. This answer does not hold up: the next step challenges it, and step 12 replaces the whole approach.

phrases.english: We are speaking of one tet.
phrases.notes: That פסוק has several ט's, but "טוב" has just one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7 by narrowing the case to a single ט.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ט could hint either at "טוב" or at the destruction פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a single ט is a good sign, matching "טוב"; the destruction פסוק has many ט's.

steps.title: A single ט can also begin a bad פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 8. A פסוק about impurity also starts with a single ט.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you could say a single ט hints to "Her impurity is in her skirts"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. A single ט could just as easily remind us of a bad פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the good sign is a single ט, like in טוב. But "טֻמְאָתָהּ בְּשׁוּלֶיהָ" from איכה also opens with one ט. So "one ט" alone does not prove the sign is good.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead / you could just as well say

phrases.english: Say instead: "Her impurity is in her skirts"!
phrases.notes: איכה 1:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the single-ט answer of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a single ט points to טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bad פסוק also opens with a single ט, so the sign could be bad

steps.title: We mean ט together with ב
steps.stepSummary: The good sign is a ט followed by a ב, which spells the start of טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about ט together with ב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the good sign. It is seeing ט and ב together, the first two letters of טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טֻמְאָתָהּ starts with ט and then מ, so it does not match. Only ט-ב spells the beginning of טוב.

phrases.english: We mean ט together with ב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any single ט is the sign
steps.terutzMaskana: Only ט followed by ב, as in טוב

steps.title: ט-ב can also begin a bad פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. "טָבְעוּ בָּאָרֶץ שְׁעָרֶיהָ" also starts with ט-ב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you could say it hints to "Her gates are sunk into the ground"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the new answer. There is a sad פסוק that also starts with ט and ב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טָבְעוּ ("sunk") begins with ט-ב, exactly like טוב. So even the narrower rule does not prove the sign is good.

phrases.english: Say instead: "Her gates are sunk into the ground"!
phrases.notes: איכה 2:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ט-ב answer of step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ט-ב points to טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bad פסוק also opens with ט-ב

steps.title: The תורה first uses ט for good
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reason. The first ט in the whole תורה is in the word טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is that the תורה first uses ט for something good. From "בראשית" until "And God saw the light" (that it was טוב), no ט is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the letter-matching approach. It gives a better reason: the very first ט in the תורה appears in the word טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Matching ט to one word always fails, because bad words can start the same way. Instead, the sign follows the letter's first appearance in the תורה, and that is in "כִּי טוֹב" in בראשית 1:4.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק opened with it / first used it

steps.whatToRemember: ט is a good sign in a dream because the first ט in the תורה is in the word טוב, describing the light.

phrases.english: Rather, since the פסוק first opened with it
phrases.notes: "It" means the letter ט.

phrases.english: for good, at the very beginning –
for from "In the beginning" until "And God saw the light,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:4. The פסוק goes on "כִּי טוֹב," that it was good.

phrases.english: no ט is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הוֹאִיל וּפָתַח בּוֹ הַכָּתוּב לְטוֹבָה תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by replacing the whole approach
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason replacing the earlier ones
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ט is good because it matches the start of טוב
steps.terutzMaskana: ט is good because its first use in the תורה is in טוב

steps.title: Seeing a הספד in a dream is a good sign
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that dreaming of a הספד means Heaven had pity on the dreamer and saved him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: One who sees a eulogy in his dream, Heaven had pity on him and saved him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new dream teaching is brought. It sounds scary, but it is actually a good sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think dreaming of a הספד is a bad sign. But the word הספד is read as a hint to חסו (they had pity) and פדאוהו (they saved him). Heaven spared the person from a real הספד.
steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT a bad sign. The scary-sounding dream is read as a sign of rescue.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who sees a eulogy in his dream –
Heaven had pity on him, and they saved him.
phrases.notes: The letters of הספד hint at these two words: חסו and פדאוהו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another dream teaching in the same theme
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A הספד seen in a dream means Heaven spared the person

steps.title: Only when the word is seen written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the teaching. It applies only when the word הספד is seen in writing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only when it is seen in writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hint works through the letters of the word הספד. So the good sign applies only when the dreamer sees the word written, not an actual funeral scene.

phrases.english: This applies only in writing.
phrases.notes: He saw the word הספד written, not a real eulogy happening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the teaching of step 13
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The good sign of הספד is only when the word is seen written

steps.title: Rooster, peacock and pheasant are כלאים
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה: wild animals and birds also have כלאים. ריש לקיש says רבי taught here that rooster, peacock and pheasant are כלאים with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And so too wild animals and birds are like them." ריש לקיש said: Here רבי taught that a rooster, a peacock and a pheasant are כלאים with one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the dream discussion and goes back to the משנה. ריש לקיש gives an example of כלאים among birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the כלאים rules for domestic animals also apply to wild animals and birds. ריש לקיש points out that a rooster, a peacock and a pheasant count as different kinds. So they may not be paired together.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a concrete example showing that the כלאים rules really do apply to birds, not only to domestic animals.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן חַיָּה וָעוֹף כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: "And so too wild animals and birds are like them, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. "Like them" means like domestic animals, for the כלאים rules.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: Here Rabbi taught:
phrases.notes: "רבי" is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

phrases.english: A rooster, a peacock, and a pheasant –
are forbidden mixtures with one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the dream discussion and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rooster, peacock and pheasant are כלאים with each other

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש needed to teach that rooster, peacock and pheasant are כלאים, since they are clearly different birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the teaching from Step 15. These three birds look completely different, so why would anyone need to be told they are כלאים? This sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teaching in the גמרא is supposed to add something new. If a rule seems self-evident, the גמרא asks what the new point is. The challenge targets the need for the statement, not its truth.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. The גמרא asks why a statement was needed at all.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: rooster, peacock and pheasant are plainly different birds, so why teach that they are כלאים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the ruling of ריש לקיש in Step 15 teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: The teaching that rooster, peacock and pheasant are כלאים with each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The birds are visibly different species, so the ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: The birds are raised together
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא explains that people raise these birds together, so we might have thought they count as one species. The teaching tells us they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא said: The new point is that they are raised together. You might have said that makes them one species, so the teaching tells us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חביבא answers the challenge. He explains why the teaching was needed after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since these birds are raised together and live side by side, one might think they count as one kind for כלאים. The teaching shows that living together does not make them one species. The physical difference between the birds still decides.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. This introduces a mistaken idea we could have had.
It teaches us. This introduces the new point.

steps.whatToRemember: Animals that are raised together are still separate species for כלאים if they really are different kinds.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥaviva said:
Because they are raised together,
you might say: it is one species;
so it teaches us that they are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲבִיבָא: מִשּׁוּם דְּרָבוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) that the teaching rules out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since they are raised together, they would count as one species.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being raised together does not make them one species. They are כלאים.

steps.title: Domestic goose and wild goose are כלאים
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the domestic goose and the wild goose are כלאים with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The goose and the wild goose are כלאים with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a new ruling about birds. Two kinds of goose that look similar still count as separate species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes further than the last teaching. These two birds look much alike and share the name 'goose', but שמואל still treats them as two species. The next steps ask what makes them different.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixed kinds with each other

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
A goose and a wild goose
are diverse kinds with each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case to the topic of כלאים among birds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The domestic goose and the wild goose are separate species for כלאים.

steps.title: A different beak can't be the reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן asks for שמואל's reason. If it is the longer or shorter beak, then Persian and Arabian camels, whose necks differ in thickness, would also be כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן objected: What is the reason? If it is because one has a long beak and the other a short beak, then a Persian camel and an Arabian camel, where one has a thick neck and the other a thin neck, should also be כלאים with each other!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן challenges שמואל's ruling. He shows that a small body difference like beak length cannot be enough to make two species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He guesses the obvious reason, the difference in beak length, and then knocks it down by comparison. Persian and Arabian camels also differ in one body feature, the neck, yet everyone agrees they are one species. So a difference in size of one body part cannot decide the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it. This introduces a strong challenge.
If you say. This introduces a suggested reason that will be rejected.
But if so. This introduces the problem that follows from the suggestion.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan objects to this:
What is the reason?
If you say it is because this one's beak is long
and that one's beak is short;
but if so,
a Persian camel and an Arabian camel,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהַאי אַלִּים קוֹעֵיהּ וְהַאי קַטִּין קוֹעֵיהּ,
phrases.english: where this one's neck is thick and that one's neck is thin,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּהָווּ כִּלְאַיִם זֶה בָּזֶה?!
phrases.english: would they also be diverse kinds with each other?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind שמואל's ruling in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumed reason for שמואל's ruling, which is the difference in beak length.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Comparison to camels. A difference in size of one body part does not make separate species, since Persian and Arabian camels are one species.

steps.title: אביי: the male's body is different
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a different reason. In one kind of goose the male's testicles are outside, and in the other they are inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: In this one the testicles are on the outside, and in that one the testicles are on the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends שמואל's ruling with a better reason. The two geese differ in their reproductive body, not just in beak size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the beak reason is dropped. אביי points to a basic difference in how the body is built, which is more than a size difference. So the camel comparison no longer works against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This drops the earlier reason and gives a new one.
On the outside / on the inside

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
This one's testicles are on the outside,
and that one's testicles are on the inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: זֶה בֵּיצָיו מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 with a new reason for שמואל's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new reason for the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The geese differ only in beak length, which is not enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ in the male's reproductive body, which is a real species difference.

steps.title: רב פפא: the female lays differently
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives another reason. One kind of goose carries one egg at a time inside its body, and the other carries several.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This one carries one egg at a time in its ovary, and that one carries several eggs in its ovary.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a second way to defend שמואל. He points to a difference in the female instead of the male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like אביי, רב פפא finds a basic difference in how the birds reproduce. This time the difference is in how many eggs the female carries at once. Either way, the two geese are shown to be truly different species.

keyTerms.meaning: Ovary, the place where eggs form

steps.whatToRemember: The domestic and wild goose are כלאים because of real differences in how they reproduce, not because of beak size.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This one carries one egg in its ovary,
and that one carries several eggs in its ovary.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הָא טְעוּנָה חֲדָא בֵּיעֲתָא בְּשִׁיחְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 19, alongside the answer of אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the same ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The geese differ only in beak length.
steps.terutzMaskana: The females differ in how many eggs they carry at once, so they are separate species.

steps.title: Crossbreeding sea creatures earns lashes
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes ריש לקיש: someone who crossbreeds two species of sea creatures gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said in the name of ריש לקיש: One who crossbreeds two species from the sea gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling moves the topic of כלאים from land and air to the sea. The איסור of crossbreeding applies to sea creatures too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we discussed animals and birds. ריש לקיש teaches that sea creatures are also included, and the punishment is the full תורה punishment of מלקות. This raises the question of where the תורה teaches it, which comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: One who mates animals, or crossbreeds them

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Reish Lakish said:
One who crossbreeds two species that are in the sea
is lashed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הַמַּרְבִּיעַ שְׁנֵי מִינִים שֶׁבַּיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic: כלאים among sea creatures.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crossbreeding two sea species is a Torah איסור punished with מלקות.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the תורה teaches that crossbreeding sea creatures is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of ריש לקיש's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's פסוק about crossbreeding speaks of 'your animals'. For a punishment of מלקות, we need a clear source in the תורה that includes sea creatures.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? Here it means: what is the Torah source?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source of the ruling in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that forbids crossbreeding sea creatures.

steps.title: Learned from the word 'according to its species'
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה, in the name of עולא, says it is learned by a גזירה שוה. The word למינהו is used for land creatures and also for sea creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of עולא: It is learned from 'according to its species' and 'according to its species' from dry land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source. Since the same word appears for land creatures and sea creatures, the rule for land creatures applies to sea creatures as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה links two places in the תורה that use the same word. Land creatures may not be crossbred, and the word למינהו connects them to sea creatures. So the same איסור, and the same מלקות, applies in the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, meaning it is learned from
A teaching learned from the same word used in two places

steps.whatToRemember: The איסור of crossbreeding reaches sea creatures through a גזירה שוה of the word למינהו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said in the name of Ulla:
It is learned from "according to its species" and "according to its species" from dry land.
phrases.notes: Both words come from the creation story in בראשית א. The same word used for land creatures teaches about sea creatures.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא: אָתְיָא לְמִינֵהוּ לְמִינֵהוּ מִיַּבָּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23 with a Torah source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה between the word למינהו used for land creatures and for sea creatures.

steps.title: Driving a goat and a fish together
steps.stepSummary: רחבה asks whether someone who drives with a goat and a שיבוטא fish together breaks the ban on working two species together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחבה asked: If someone drives with a goat and a שיבוטא fish together, what is the law? Do we say that since the goat never goes into the sea and the fish never comes onto land, he has done nothing wrong? Or perhaps, since right now he is driving them together, he is guilty?
steps.whatsHappening: רחבה asks a new question. A person drives with a goat on the shore and a fish in the water at the same time. Is this forbidden כלאים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that כלאים rules apply to sea creatures too. So רחבה asks about a mix of one land animal and one sea animal. One side says they never really work together, since each stays in its own place. The other side says that right now he is still driving both together.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question that is not yet answered (a בעיא)
One who drives or leads animals
Do we say this, or perhaps that? (sets up the two sides of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about crossbreeding, which was the topic of steps 22 to 24. Here the question is about making two species work together.

phrases.english: Rachava asked:
One who drives with a goat and a shibbuta, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Picture a wagon pulled by a goat on the shore and a fish in the water at the same time.

phrases.english: Do we say:
since the goat does not go down into the sea,
and the shibbuta does not come up onto dry land,
he has done nothing;
or perhaps,
now, at any rate, he is driving them together?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea that sea creatures have כלאים rules, and applies it to a mix of a land animal and a sea animal working together.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does driving a land animal and a sea animal together, each in its own place, count as forbidden working with two species?

steps.title: Wheat in ארץ ישראל and barley outside
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges the question: by that logic, sowing a joined wheat and barley seed half in ארץ ישראל and half outside should also make him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged this: If so, then if someone joined wheat and barley in his hand and sowed the wheat in ארץ ישראל and the barley outside ארץ ישראל, would he also be liable?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the second side of רחבה's question. He gives a similar case that seems obviously not forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If driving together counts even when each species is in a different place, then sowing two seeds together across the border should count too. But that seems clearly not to be כלאים. So רבינא suggests the question has an obvious answer: no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (introduces a result that seems impossible)
Would it also be this way?

phrases.english: Ravina challenged it:
But if so,
if he joined wheat and barley in his hand,
and sowed the wheat in the Land,
and the barley outside the Land,
would he also be liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second side of רחבה's question by comparing it to a seed case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The side of רחבה's question that says driving the two together may be forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two species in two different places can count as together, then wheat in ארץ ישראל and barley outside should be liable too. That seems clearly wrong, so the question seems pointless.

steps.title: The two cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבינא's comparison: outside ארץ ישראל there is no ban on mixed seeds, but land and sea are both places where the ban on mixed species applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: How can you compare? There, ארץ ישראל is a place where the ban applies, and outside ארץ ישראל is not. Here, both the land and the sea are places where the ban applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבינא and shows that his comparison does not work. So רחבה's question is still a real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the seed case, the barley is planted where there is no seed ban at all, so of course there is no liability. In the goat and fish case, each animal is in a place where the ban on mixing species does apply. So רבינא's case does not answer רחבה's question.

keyTerms.meaning: A place where the obligation or ban applies
This one and that one, both

steps.whatToRemember: רחבה's question stands. A goat on land and a fish in the sea are each in a place where the ban on mixing species applies, unlike a seed planted outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: They said: How can you compare?!
There, the Land is a place of obligation,
and outside the Land is not a place of obligation;
phrases.notes: The ban on sowing mixed seeds only applies in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: here, both this one and that one are places of obligation.
phrases.notes: Both the land, where the goat is, and the sea, where the fish is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבינא's challenge and keeps רחבה's question alive.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רבינא's comparison. It does not decide רחבה's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the seed case, one half is in a place with no ban at all. In the goat and fish case, both places have the ban, so the cases are different.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing שור שנגח את הפרה
steps.stepSummary: The פרק שור שנגח את הפרה ends with the הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, שור שנגח את הפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק called שור שנגח את הפרה. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן formula says we will come back to this פרק. It closes the chapter that began with an ox goring a cow and ended with these questions about כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
The ox that gored the cow (the name of this פרק)

phrases.english: We will return to you,
The Ox That Gored the Cow

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ שׁוֹר שֶׁנָּגַח אֶת הַפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק שור שנגח את הפרה is finished.
